chunks.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي رَحِمَهُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلْعَلَاءِ بْنِ ٱلْفُضَيْلِ عَنِ ٱلصَّادِقِ ع قَالَ

translations.en: My father narrated to us, may Allah have mercy on him, from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

chunks.arabic_text: مَنْ أَحَبَّ كَافِرًا فَقَدْ أَبْغَضَ ٱللَّهَ وَ مَنْ أَبْغَضَ كَافِرًا فَقَدْ أَحَبَّ ٱللَّهَ

translations.en: He who loves a disbeliever has hated Allah, and he who hates a disbeliever has loved Allah.

chunks.arabic_text: ثُمَّ قَالَ ع صَدِيقُ عَدُوِّ ٱللَّهِ عَدُوُّ ٱللَّهِ

translations.en: Then he (peace be upon him) added: The friend of Allah's enemy is Allah's enemy.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the principle of *al-wala' wa al-barra'* (allegiance and disavowal), positing that affection for a disbeliever inherently signifies a diminution of love for Allah, while disavowal of them affirms divine love. This hadith serves as a foundational text in Shia theology for understanding how interpersonal relations with non-Muslims reflect one's spiritual state. The concluding maxim reinforces the concept that proximity to Allah's adversaries necessitates a corresponding enmity towards them, a key tenet in distinguishing the faithful from the disbelievers.
en.seo_question: What is the relationship between loving a disbeliever and hating Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
